_note: Path prefixes containing '*' use glob-aware matching (fnmatch-style): '*/docs/dev/overnight/' matches that directory under any worktree. A prefix starting with '/' is anchored at the project root. The shared protected list is the SOLE catch-all for /.claude/ — DO NOT add broad '/.claude/' to denied prefixes; use only the explicit subdirs above so legitimate worktree paths remain writable. Allow prefixes name directories (ending in '/') or wildcards (ending in '*'), and the /dev/null, /dev/stderr and /dev/stdout devices, never the file of an artifact: hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py derives an artifact's write permission from the session's dispatch records (P1b E3). A path a dispatch's obligation declares (with the producer question it names and what the template it was dispatched from declares in the current command files) is written by that dispatch only, whatever these rows allow, and the role's deny prefixes still apply to it; an undeclared path keeps these rows. Deny prefixes grant nothing and all stay. cp-state files have one writer, scripts/spec-check.py (pretool-cp-state-write-guard.py). The managed scratch namespace '*/.claude/scratch/' is granted to every role; raw /tmp and /var/tmp are denied for every role, including one holding '*', except that role's own exact temp entries ('*/tmp/claude-scratch/<role>/', '*/var/tmp/codex-outputs/', '<state dir>/agentic-commit/<role>/'). A JSON prefix cannot express actor identity, so raw-temp denial and owner-vs-sibling scratch exactness are enforced behaviorally by hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py; these rows are the declaration, not the sole enforcement. policy_version 8 (P1b): every allow prefix that named an artifact's file went, with user.allowed_path_prefixes, which nothing read. /clean's approved actions (P9-4): while a human-typed /clean's span is active, what its owner approved (the main agent's Write of docs/clean/user-approvals-<id>.json recorded in the session transcript: a move's or rename's destination, a fix_style file) is written by that span's cleaner only, and the project's root README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md by its rule-inspector only; that write skips the role's allow prefixes and its source and test denials, never _shared_protected_path_prefixes, and no other caller, the main agent included, writes those paths in that span (hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py, _check_clean_writes). write_carveout_prefixes (policy_version 9, owner decision 2026-11-17): a row may name project-root-anchored directories ('/' first and last, no '*', no '.' or '..' segment) its role writes although a deny prefix holds them; a target is inside one only when its normalised path AND its realpath both lie under that directory (taken under the project's logical path or its realpath, never the directory's own realpath) and an existing file there has one hard link, so '..', a symlink out or a hard link to a file elsewhere stays under the deny prefixes; such a target passes the row's allow list and the deny prefixes the carve-out sits under, and every other deny prefix still applies (hooks/lib/policy_registry.py, _write_denial). A Bash target that the same command first makes as a link, copy or move destination (the path or a directory above it) gets no carve-out, since the realpath is read before the command runs (hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py, _restaged_targets). Only qa holds one: '/reports/' and '/tests/reports/'; its '/tests/' deny keeps every other path under tests/.

user.rationale: User simulation: Playwright/read for user-flow testing; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight, codex and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits

ui-specialist.rationale: UI specialist DESIGN_MODE: read + screenshot; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight, codex and scratch directories; forbid app-source writes and protected infrastructure

ba.rationale: BA: analysis; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares and the producer question that obligation names (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its research, codex, overnight and scratch directories; no code/agent/hook writes

dev.rationale: Dev: write per files_to_modify/files_to_create from BA context; orchestrator-level enforcement of scope. A path another dispatch's obligation declares is that dispatch's alone, whatever '*' allows (pretool-tool-policy.py)

qa.rationale: QA: read + verify; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its codex, overnight and scratch directories, and its report and evidence files under the project's reports/ and tests/reports/ (write_carveout_prefixes, owner decision 2026-11-17); no app/source/test-code edits: the rest of tests/ stays denied

pm.rationale: PM: read + plan/triage/retro; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares under the overnight directory (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its codex and scratch directories; no implementation

architect.rationale: Architect: read + analyze; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight, codex and scratch directories

product-owner.rationale: Product-owner: business-logic analysis; writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight, codex and scratch directories

cleaner.rationale: cleaner: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; while a human-typed /clean's span is active, its cleaner (dispatched after the owner's answer) also writes what that request's approvals approve: each move's or rename's destination and each fix_style file (pretool-tool-policy.py derives it from the main agent's Write of docs/clean/user-approvals-<id>.json recorded in the session transcript; no other caller writes those paths); no other source/protected/test edits.

cleanliness-inspector.rationale: cleanliness-inspector: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

git-edge-case-analyst.rationale: git-edge-case-analyst: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

prompt-inspector.rationale: prompt-inspector: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

rule-inspector.rationale: rule-inspector: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; dispatched in a human-typed /clean's active span, it also writes the project's root README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md (/clean Step 4; no other caller writes them in that span); no other source/protected/test edits.

style-inspector.rationale: style-inspector: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

test-writer.rationale: test-writer (spec-20260518-225715 §5.2): generates pytest skeleton tests from BA-produced acceptance-criteria JSON under tests/generated/ and writes what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record); explicitly forbidden from src/app/lib and all protected /.claude/ subdirs. Read access is broad (analyses AC JSON, spec files, existing tests for archive/idempotency keying).

test-executor.rationale: test-executor: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

test-validator.rationale: test-validator: non-core specialist may read/analyze and write what its dispatch's obligation declares (pretool-tool-policy.py derives that permission from the dispatch record), plus its overnight and scratch directories; no source/protected/test edits.

spec.rationale: spec: may write the spec folders and scratch only; the views directory its dispatch's obligation declares is its alone (pretool-tool-policy.py); no source/protected/test edits.

changelog-analyst.rationale: changelog-analyst: git commit operations; reads dev-artifacts, stages and commits source changes via Bash (git add/commit). Its Write tool writes the message file of its own `git commit -F`, a scratch input, under its scratch directory, and in bulk mode the docs/dev close annotation; its fd-9 lock is a redirect under /tmp/agentic-commit/locks/; the push-gate token is written by scripts/write-push-gate-token.py, never by Write; no write access to protected infra

push-analyst.rationale: push-analyst: pre-push git read-only analysis; reads commits-to-push range, sensitive file patterns, and divergence; writes nonce-keyed grant to <state dir>/agentic-commit/push-analyst/ (role-specific directory only, no broad /tmp/*; the /tmp entry is the default state dir's exception to the raw-temp denial, the */ entry a CLAUDE_STATE_DIR outside the temp roots); no write access to protected infra

merge-analyst.rationale: merge-analyst: pre-merge git read-only analysis; reads branch divergence, diff stat, conflict markers, and overnight-state for consistency validation; writes one nonce-keyed grant (60s expiry) with the Write tool to <state dir>/agentic-commit/merge-analyst/, checked on that Write by posttool-allowlist-consume.py (lib/merge_grant.py) and read by /merge (role-specific directory only, no broad /tmp/*; the /tmp entry is the default state dir's exception to the raw-temp denial, the */ entry a CLAUDE_STATE_DIR outside the temp roots); no write access to protected infra

pull-analyst.rationale: pull-analyst: post-pull advisory analysis only; reads new-commits range and semantic risk indicators (dependency manifests, schema files, API surface, CI/CD); Write tool excluded to enforce advisory-only contract — pull-analyst writes no grant and blocks nothing; no write access to protected infra

graphify.rationale: graphify: /dev Step 9 enrichment subagent; runs graphify-enrich.py via Bash, which writes the task's run record and focused subgraph under .claude/dev-registry/<task_id>/graphify/ and never the context (the graph cache is graphify-maintain.py's). Its Write grant is scoped to that graphify sub-directory, not the whole dev-registry, so it cannot author peer artifacts. No Skill/Edit (graphify.md uses neither). No write access to protected infra.

built_in_agents._note: Claude Code's own agent types that a dispatch may name and no role row covers. They are not roles: hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py reads only "roles" and leaves these agents unrestricted, as before. A row here declares which tools the agent type carries, so a rule that depends on whether a dispatched agent can write (hooks/pretool-gitignore-preflight.py) reads it from this file; an agent type named neither here nor under "roles" (general-purpose, a plugin agent) counts as able to write.

Explore.rationale: Claude Code's read-only codebase search agent: it has no Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit tool.

_read_only_and_bookkeeping_tools_note: Every role's allowed_tools names the CLI's read-only and bookkeeping tools (OB-L22): Read, Grep and Glob (search, read-only); TodoWrite and its older read-only TodoRead, and TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList and TaskUpdate, which the CLI offers in TodoWrite's place while CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS is on (the agent's own task list); TaskOutput and its older name BashOutput (read the caller's own background task's output); TaskStop and its older name KillShell (stop the caller's own background task, starting none); ToolSearch (loads a deferred tool's schema; that tool's own call is still judged by these rows). None writes a file, runs a command, reaches the network or dispatches an agent; Grep and Glob take no target here, so denied_path_prefixes binds Read only, as before (hooks/tests/test_tool_policy_readonly_bookkeeping.py).
_docs_and_web_tools_note: Context7, WebFetch and WebSearch (OB-L23, owner decision): dev, qa, ba and the four specialists (architect, product-owner, ui-specialist, user; agents/shared/specialist-protocol.md) name WebFetch, WebSearch and Context7's read-only documentation tools, resolve-library-id, query-docs and its older name get-library-docs, under the server prefix mcp__context7__ and the plugin prefix mcp__plugin_context7_context7__. They are named exactly, never by a wildcard, so a tool the server adds later stays refused until a row names it. They read documentation and the web; none writes a file, runs a command or dispatches an agent. Every other role keeps none of them, and no row names any mcp__github__ tool, so GitHub writes stay refused for every role (hooks/tests/test_tool_policy_docs_and_web.py).
